decision: ACCEPT the vendored v1 blind-client browser artifact (470a48af/aaf29c82/09bd04c8, 2026-07-16) for the Peerit bounded public-test canary, with WIRE_TUPLE_DRIFT disclosed in every artifact.
basis: The deployed relay build (c9ddd235/199ba15d/fa54012c, 2026-07-24, v2 authority) is the v1 tuple PLUS disabled FORWARD schemas only; the v1 client speaks a valid subset of the deployed authority, and the baseline LIMITED_PUBLIC_TEST_V1 profile (DESCRIBE/CELL/INBOX/CORE) sits entirely inside that subset. FORWARD is disabled, so the drift is additive, not breaking.
Re-pin to the relay's matching v3 artifact is honestly impossible: it declares runtimeReady/realBrowserEvidenceAccepted/authorizesRelease=false.

Empirical proof: two-relay CELL write/readback through the Peerit client passed on both relays (signed receipts, byte-exact readback under each relay's own key); restart recovery passed; boundary proof zero app plaintext markers in 46 relay-visible requests.
The catalogue flip (config/blind-public-test-bind.scaffold.json -> bound: true, canary) stands; the revert-by-one-commit path remains available if this decision is ever revisited.
boundary: bounded public-test canary on two owner-operated failure domains; NOT GA; NOT independent operators; no seed-publish (owner review pending); relay-side placeholder profile-hash rotation + fresh re-probe is a later relay pass
followups: relay-side placeholder profile-hash rotation (DAL1-IAR-P2-1) then fresh re-probe
